result.keywords: This article examines archival mapmaking practices in fictional coastal municipalities and how lunar tide annotations shaped navigation records, municipal folklore, and museum curation. It compares hand-drawn atlases, harbor ledgers, and ceremonial tide charts, proposing a taxonomy for interpreting symbolic shoreline markers across dispersed civic collections. The study focuses on cultural geography, historical documentation, and interpretive preservation rather than engineering or computing methods.
result.title: Glass Harbor: Cartography of Lunar Tides in Coastal Archives.
